rationale: B wins because it turns the strongest claim into a reporting assignment, not a vibe: “The installer bottleneck: a home battery that claims it skips the rewiring” comes with install-hours, permitting, warranty, installer-network, and price-per-kWh proof. A has the same bones, but “Anker is betting homeowners skip home batteries because of the installation job, not the price” overstates a causal thesis the update does not prove. B also keeps the consumer angle honest by saying it needs “one real US household...with before-and-after bill figures,” instead of inventing the customer or killing the beat entirely.
gaps_in_A: “Anker just set the timeline” is too grand for one launch. Without market data or comparable moves, Anker entered the category; it did not set the clock for it.

“homeowners skip home batteries because of the installation job, not the price” invents a causal hierarchy. The update gives a no-major-rewiring claim, not evidence that installation beats price as the adoption blocker.
Some beats are still soft: “an energy tech reporter at a trade outlet or business publication” and “a consumer tech or business reporter” are usable, but not as sharp as they should be.
It refuses “Peak-rate bill-cutting as a personal finance angle” too completely. With a named household, bills, rate plan, installed cost, and warranty, that is a legitimate consumer-finance story.
gaps_in_B: “What a homeowner is actually buying when they buy backup power” is labeled “customer-story” while admitting it needs “at least one real US household.” That is a parked angle, not pitch-ready material.

“Soft costs and electrician scarcity are the recurring problem in that beat” imports outside market context. Probably true, but the supplied update does not prove it; source it before it goes near a reporter.
“changes the price floor of home storage” is smart but fragile because pricing and capacity are only partially disclosed. Keep it as a question until Anker gives dollars per usable kilowatt-hour.
The next step points to “newsjack-detector,” which is fussy for a straight launch. The cleaner move is the one B buries afterward: run journalist-fit-check on the installer angle first.
